_comment: WHAT THE APP ACTUALLY NEEDS TODAY. Attach this as-is.
These two actions are the entire AWS surface of the application. Verify
that claim rather than trusting it: grep the codebase for boto3 clients
and you will find rekognition and sts, nothing else.
Both actions are required. DetectFaces runs FIRST as a quality gate - one
face, sharp enough, facing the camera - and CompareFaces only runs if that
passes. Granting CompareFaces alone fails every punch before it compares.
Resource must be "*": Rekognition's CompareFaces and DetectFaces do not
support resource-level permissions, so there is nothing narrower to scope
to. This is a limitation of the service, not laziness here.
NOT INCLUDED, ON PURPOSE: S3. This policy used to carry s3:PutObject and
friends for photo storage, which caused a reasonable 'do you actually need
all this?' from the person granting it. We do not call S3 at all - photos
are files on local disk (app/services/storage.py). Add the block at the
bottom of this file only when S3Storage exists and is wired in.
Attach to a programmatic-only IAM user created for this app (suggested
name: boxcode-hrms-api), never to a personal account - see
docs/AWS-CREDENTIALS.md for why. Better still, attach it to an EC2
instance role once deployed, so there is no long-lived key to leak.
Verify with: apps/api/.venv/bin/python scripts/check_aws.py
